chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:
It has reached me that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would sometimes enter the bathhouse deliberately to wax his armpit alone.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: The bathhouse, a place for ritual and social bathing

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams remove their armpit hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s deliberate practice of grooming in the bathhouse, underscoring the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition) and the importance of personal hygiene as an act of worship. By specifying the armpit, the hadith reinforces the Sunnah of removing underarm hair, a key component of ritual purity (*taharah*) and social cleanliness in Islamic tradition. This practice reflects the balance between spiritual devotion and physical well-being, encouraging believers to maintain neatness as a reflection of inner purity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,
‘It has reached me that Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> would sometimes enter the bathhouse deliberately to wax his<sup>asws</sup> armpit alone’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “
I am informed that abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, enters the bathhouse only to apply lime paste to his underarms alone.’”
